_comment: The landing page in English, and the file the other three are checked against.
Values are HTML: they carry the links, <code> and emphasis that belong to the
sentence, because where a link falls inside a sentence is the sentence's
business and moves when it is translated. Everything structural — the
sections, the mock, the table — stays in site/index.html.
What is deliberately absent: the game names, platform names and the summary
in the picture. Those are RomM's own metadata, which the demo shows in
English whatever language the interface is in, and translating them here
would make the picture claim something the demo does not do.
page.title: RomMix — a Big Picture front end for RomM
page.description: Browse your RomM library like a console dashboard — desktop, handheld or television. Download a game, play it, and your saves go back to RomM.
hero.title: Your RomM library, wherever you play.
hero.lede:
A Big Picture–style front end for your own RomM server.
Browse, download, play — saves sync back to RomM.
demo.alt: The RomMix home screen, with the game you were last playing at the top and the ones on this device below it
devices.title: Supported devices
devices.lede: One build for Linux desktops, handhelds and televisions.
devices.desk.title: At the desk
devices.desk.body: One download on any Linux desktop. Keyboard, mouse and controller all work.
devices.hands.title: In your hands
devices.hands.body: On a Steam Deck or any Linux handheld. Add the launcher script to Steam as a non-Steam game.
devices.room.title: Across the room
devices.room.body: Runs under gamescope and scales up on a 4K screen. Sign in by scanning a code with your phone.
features.title: Features
features.shelves: Shelves for recent, installed and favourite games
features.collections: Your RomM collections, and the ones RomM builds itself
features.downloads: Downloads land in your emulator's own ROM folder
features.queue: Downloads you can pause and resume, checked when they arrive
features.multidisc: Multi-disc sets unpacked and launched as one game
features.saves: Saves and states synced both ways
features.marks: Favourites, progress and play time saved to RomM
features.offline: Offline mode — play downloaded games with no connection
features.resume: Downloads and unsent saves resume when you are back online
features.bios: BIOS files installed from your own server
features.emulators: Emulators installed and assigned by RomMix
features.preflight: A pre-flight check that finds problems before you play
features.signin: Sign in by scanning a code with your phone
features.controller: Controller-driven and fullscreen, desk to television
emulators.title: Supported emulators
emulators.lede: RomMix picks which one runs each system, and Emulators → Platforms lets you change it.
emulators.retrodeck: 79 systems, the NES to the PS3
emulators.emudeck: 74 systems, the NES to the Switch and 360
getting.title: Download
getting.lede: Requires Linux, a RomM server at version 5 or newer, and one of the emulators above. Take the AppImage from the releases page and run it — choose x86_64 or arm64 depending on your machine's architecture.
getting.note: No version in the file name: updates are written over that same file.
getting.steamBody: Download rommix-steam.sh from the same release, keep it beside the AppImage, and add the script as the non-Steam game — not the AppImage itself.
getting.steamNote: Steam cannot launch an AppImage directly. The README covers building RomMix, and emulators that will not start.
footer.disclaimer: RomMix is MIT-licensed, and is not affiliated with RomM, the emulators it launches, or any console maker or game publisher. It ships no games: the covers here and the demo library come from RomM's public demo, homebrew and freeware throughout.
